newsitem.title: USA: W.African, Latam crudes abound on U.S. Gulf Coast.
newsitem.headline: W.African, Latam crudes abound on U.S. Gulf Coast.

text.p: Offers of West African and Latin American crudes abounded on the U.S. Gulf Coast Tuesday although buying interest was limited, traders said.
Buyers' lackluster interest was attributed to continued refinery turnarounds, weak margins, a preference for cheaper domestic grades and an overhang of February barrels.
Traders noted that plenty of West African crude, particularly Cabinda, is available.
Six full fob cargoes of Cabinda are on offer between March 10 and March 30, one East Coast trader said.
Other West African crudes on offer include Qua Iboe, Escravos, Forcados and Brass River.
North Sea crudes remain scarce on the Gulf Coast despite the gradually widening spread between benchmarks West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent.
The April spread was around $1.75-80 a barrel Tuesday afternoon, up about 15 cents from last Friday but still not high enough to generate transatlantic business.
Brent to the Gulf Coast for early April arrival was talked around April WTI minus 25-35 cents a barrel.
From Latin America, traders noted that several March loaders of Colombian Cano Limon were moving sluggishly. The asking range was around WTI minus $2.05 a barrel, traders said.
Colombian state-owned Ecopetrol is tendering a March 4-5 Vasconia cargo, while a European equity producer is gearing up to begin marketing an end-March Cusiana, traders said.
Activity is likely to remain slow this week because many traders are attending annual IP week festivities in London.
